text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**

Founder of Amalgamated Wireless Australia (AWA) Sir ERNEST FISK was born in 1886. He made the first international test transmission in 1918 from his home. The Fisk Radiola was named after him and also AWA'a Victorian headquarters at Fiskville.
American physicist ERNEST LAWRENCE, who invented the colour television picture tube, was born in 1901. He won the Nobel Prize for physics in 1939.
A pioneer of Australian country music TEX MORTON (ROBERT LANE) was born in 1916. One of his biggest hits was "The Goondiwindi Grey".
American actress and former swimming champion ESTHER WILLIAMS was born in 1923.
Jazz man DON BURROWS, a great from the Australian music scene, was born in 1928.

Australian businessman BOB ANSETT was born in Hamilton in Victoria in 1933. The son of aviation pioneer, Sir REGINALD ANSETT, BOB went to live in the United States when he was 10 years old. He returned to Australia in 1965, flat broke.

Australian radio broadcaster JOHN LAWS was born in 1935. He is said to be the highest-paid talkback host in the world. He was born RICHARD JOHN LAWS in Wau, New Guinea, and began his radio career in Bendigo at the age of 20.
American actor DUSTIN HOFFMAN was born in 1937. His varied film career has included successful movies such as "The Graduate", "Rain Man", "Accidental Hero" and "Midnight Cowboy".
Dr Hook's drummer JAY DAVID was born in 1942.
British motor racing champion NIGEL MANSELL was born in 1953.
British guitarist and songwriter CHRIS FOREMAN was born in 1958. His nickname is "CHRISSIE-BOY". He was a founding member of Madness in 1976.
**EVENTS**
1788 : The first cattle, five cows and two bulls, arrived
in Australia. They were off-loaded in Sydney and it's believed that they were either eaten or wandered into the bush. The first substantial consignment of 200 cattle arrived in Hobart in 1804.
1806 : WILLIAM BLIGH became the fourth Governor of New
South Wales. He survived the 1789 mutiny when he was captain of HMS Bounty on a voyage from Tahiti to the West Indies.
1900 : The first DAVIS CUP was held between the USA and
the United Kingdom at Brookline, Massachussetts. Australian joined the competition in 1907 and won the cup 24 times in the following 70 years.
1909 : Electricity was harnessed to shear sheep for the
first time in Australia. New South Wales grazier R.S. FALKINER invented the shearing device which was demonstrated at sheep stud sales.
1912 : The Westphalian pit disaster in Germany claimed
the lives of 120 miners.
1927 : The Cenotaph in Sydney's Martin Place was
dedicated to those who died in the Great War.
1935 : HITLER's propaganda machine took control of the
new German television service.
1944 : HITLER had four of his top men hanged by piano
wire for attempting to assassinate him.
1958 : A 17-year-old British singer, CLIFF RICHARD, was
signed to Columbia records.
1963 : Australia was the first nation to sign the nuclear
test ban treaty, which was also signed by the United States, USSR and Britain. The treaty banned nuclear weapons testing in the atmosphere, outer-space and underwater.
1963 : The Great Train Robbery, known as the most

audacious crime in British history, netted the gang almost three million pounds. At least 15 armed men, wearing masks, used a fake red track signal to stop the train at a secluded spot at Cheddington. The well-organised robbery targetted the special train, which was laden with banknotes on their way to be
destroyed. A full-scale inquiry into the security of the Royal Mail trains was ordered.
1964 : Rioting broke out at a Rolling Stones concert in
The Hague in Holland. Two girls had their clothes torn off in the riots.
1967 : In Bangkok, a declaration signed by foreign
ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand led to the formation of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
1968 : JOH BJELKE-PETERSEN became Premier of Queensland
after being elected unopposed as leader of the Country Party.
1973 : American vice-president SPIRO AGNEW went under
investigation for tax evasion.
1974 : RICHARD NIXON made history by being the first US
president to resign. He made an emotional address to the people on national television. Four days earlier he had admitted his involvment in the 'Watergate affair'. Members of NIXON's

re-election committee broke-in to the Democratic Party's headquarters in the Watergate building during the 1972 campaign. NIXON's deputy GERALD FORD was sworn in as the 38th president of the United States.
1990 : Iraq announced that it had annexed Kuwait as its
19th province and President BUSH sent U.S. troops to Saudi Arabia as part of a multi-national force to defend the kingdom.
1991 : British journalist JOHN McCARTHY was freed by the
Lebanese terrorist group holding him hostage.
1994 : Eleven miners were trapped underground in a
coalmine at Moura in Central Queensland.
1994 : The leaders of Jordan and Israel opened their
countries' first border crossing, cementing an end to 46 years of hostilities.
